author: Zintenka
body:
On Avicommunity slack, 99% of the staff and players are inactive as hell. It's nigh impossible to get a hold of staff members due to this fact.

Why have two slacks when it is better to have one that is general purpose? One that has staff and community channels. Making a separate community slack and a staff slack is redundant when you can just disallow players from channels in the first place.

Many players got warned when I was Jr. Mapdev for inactivity on the Avicommunity slack. Including me.

It's just... so redundant...

What's the point?

I can tell you now the staff slack and community slack will never merge, I think the reasons why are incredibly obvious.

replies.author: vladthegreat100
replies.body:
The following claims have been made for against this:

- Too many people in the slack
- Private Conversations
- Multiple Pinned Conversations
- Lost Archives
- Higher Chances of leaks

Lets go through each one:
Too many people in the slack:
Staff Members are forced anyhow to be in the community slack, so this "too many people" talk is bs, there may be a few being added anyhow.

Private Conversations:
There may be many private conversations, but you guys make it sound like it's so hard. It's legit just 3 clicks of your mouse and typing of the name of the channel, the topic and purpose which is usually one sentence.And either way, most stuff in the staff slack is private anyhow. The only non-private stuff is the map-planning, general planning for tourneys for refs, and maybe one or two more things out of 20 or so private + public channels.

Multiple Pinned Conversations:
When pinning conversations, it doesn't go globally to every channel, it legit stays in the channel that you pinned it in. And from what I've noticed in the community slack, nothing or not much has gotten pinned, so nothing to a bit more pins would be added.

Lost Archives:
Yes that may be a thing, but the community slack legit only gets 1.5K messages a EDIT: a week. That is an average of 4 messages per person. There isn't much of a difference, except the team has to either tone down on all the spam (Yeah, remember that ladder spam that happened that one day... well that's spam) So if you guys can actually follow rules that everyone else in the community slack follows, meaning not spamming ladders, then you guys should be fine with the 10K limit .

Higher Chances of Leaks:
Well lets think of it this way. You have staff members you are meant to trust. If they leak, it's either them personally telling someone else, which is exactly the same way it would be with the separate slacks, they add someone to the chat where they now have the archives of this chat, which means they just blatantly showed you they are not trust worthy, which usually warrants a demotion and a ban from past experiences with others that were falsely banned for leaks, or they accidentally say out in a public channel, where it may be pretty hard, just because they should notice that there are non-staff that had written in that chat. So leaks may be slightly higher with the accidental leak, but that's a personal fuck up that would be hard to accomplish imo. And it's not like leaking from the Administrators isn't a thing. Pastebin has a leak from 2 current Admins, and a former Admin. So atm, we may even have an Admin that leaks stuff  that was probably meant to stay confidential¯\_(ツ)_/¯

So as you can see, most "problems" that were brought up isn't really much of a problem, but a nuisance for a good 30 to one hour which can actually bring out some good. For example, actually have your staff active on the community slack. You forced everyone to join it, but in the end, maybe 10% of the staff actually use the slack. Doing that will probably bond the staff with the community even more knowing they will be forced to be active there, meaning they will communicate with us, and actually moderate channels that need moderation and answer feedbacks/calls for help in reports other than the same people.
